knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Radius Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact scalar optimality condition for annihilation of a radial block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g=\phi+\iota_{[0,+\infty)}\), where \(\phi\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex on \([0,+\infty)\). For input radius \(\rho\geq0\) and \(\lambda>0\), the radial proximal solution \[r=\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\geq0}\left\{\phi(s)+\frac{(s-\rho)^2}{2\lambda}\right\}\] satisfies \(r=0\) exactly when \(\rho/\lambda\in\partial g(0)\). If \(\phi'_+(0)\) is finite, this is equivalent to \(0\leq\rho\leq\lambda\phi'_+(0)\). For \(\phi(s)=ws\) with \(w\geq0\), the regime is \(\rho\leq\lambda w\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A radial block becomes zero exactly when its scaled input radius belongs to the constrained scalar subdifferential at zero.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex on \([0,+\infty)\).

notation.meaning: right derivative of phi at zero

children.title: Dual-Ball Projection Forms
children.top_down_role: Norm proximal mappings evaluated through dual-ball projections.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Ball Projection Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moreau decomposition of a norm proximal mapping through its dual unit ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\) be a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space, let \(\|\cdot\|\) be any norm, and let \(B_* =\{u:\|u\|_*\leq1\}\) be its dual unit ball. Since the Fenchel conjugate of \(\lambda\|\cdot\|\) is \(\iota_{\lambda B_*}\), Moreau decomposition gives, for every \(x\in\mathcal H\) and \(\lambda>0\), \[\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda\|\cdot\|}(x)=x-P_{\lambda B_*}(x).\] The projection is taken in the Hilbert norm induced by the ambient inner product, even when the penalty norm and its dual are non-Euclidean.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal mapping of any norm equals the input minus its Euclidean metric projection onto the scaled dual unit ball.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) is a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space.
\(\|\cdot\|\) is a norm with dual norm \(\|\cdot\|_*\).

ambient metric projection onto the scaled dual ball

children.title: Quadratic-Affine Proximal Family

children.title: Convex Quadratic Forms
children.top_down_role: Proximal evaluations governed by positive semidefinite quadratic structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Quadratic Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal map of a positive-semidefinite quadratic form on a real Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(Q:H\to H\) be bounded, self-adjoint, and positive semidefinite, and define \(q(y)=\tfrac12\langle y,Qy\rangle\) for \(y\in H\). For every \(x\in H\) and \(\gamma>0\), the proximal minimizer is unique and satisfies
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma q}(x)=(I+\gamma Q)^{-1}x.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal map of a positive-semidefinite quadratic form is obtained by applying the inverse of I plus gamma Q to the input.
assumptions_latex: \(Q:H\to H\) is bounded, self-adjoint, and positive semidefinite.

notation.meaning: The quadratic function mapping y to one half of the inner product of y and Qy.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard proximal formula for a bounded positive-semidefinite quadratic form

children.title: Affine Forms
children.top_down_role: Proximal effects of linear functionals with constant offsets.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form proximal map of a continuous affine functional.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, fix \(a\in H\) and \(\beta\in\mathbb R\), and set \(f(y)=\langle a,y\rangle+\beta\). For every \(x\in H\) and \(\gamma>0\),
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(x)=x-\gamma a.
\]
The additive constant \(\beta\) does not affect the minimizer. Equivalently, the proximal optimality equation is \(0=a+\gamma^{-1}(p-x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine functional shifts its argument by minus gamma times its slope; its constant term has no effect on the proximal point.

notation.meaning: Riesz representative of the affine functional's linear part.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct solution of the proximal optimality equation for an affine functional
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formula is mathematically standard, internally complete, and appropriately classified as a representation, but no inspectable source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Quadratic-Affine Combinations

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-Affine Combinations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unified proximal formula for a convex quadratic plus an affine term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(Q:H\to H\) be bounded, self-adjoint, and positive semidefinite, and define \(f(y)=\tfrac12\langle y,Qy\rangle+\langle a,y\rangle+\beta\). For \(x\in H\) and \(\gamma>0\),
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(x)=(I+\gamma Q)^{-1}(x-\gamma a).
\]
Thus proximal evaluation requires one solve with the strongly positive operator \(I+\gamma Q\); the constant \(\beta\) is immaterial.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal point of a quadratic-affine function solves one linear system whose right-hand side is shifted by the affine coefficient.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is bounded, self-adjoint, and positive semidefinite on \(H\).

children.title: Singular Quadratic Regimes
children.top_down_role: Evaluation behavior when the quadratic component is rank deficient.

knowledge_statements.title: Singular Quadratic Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of a nontrivial quadratic nullspace on proximal evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(Q:H\to H\) be bounded, self-adjoint, positive semidefinite, and possibly singular, and define \(q(y)=\tfrac12\langle y,Qy\rangle\) for \(y\in H\). For every \(x\in H\) and \(\gamma>0\), the operator \(I+\gamma Q\) is boundedly invertible and
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma q}(x)=(I+\gamma Q)^{-1}x.
\]
If \(P_{\ker Q}\) is the orthogonal projection onto \(\ker Q\), then
\[
P_{\ker Q}\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma q}(x)=P_{\ker Q}x.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even when Q is singular, I plus gamma Q is invertible, and the quadratic proximal map preserves the component of the input in the nullspace of Q.
assumptions_latex: \(Q:H\to H\) is bounded, self-adjoint, and positive semidefinite.

notation.meaning: Orthogonal projection onto the nullspace of Q.
The quadratic form generated by Q.

children.title: Finite Pointwise-Maximum Forms

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Pointwise-Maximum Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simplex dual representation of the proximal map of finitely many affine forms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m\in\mathbb N\) with \(m\ge1\), let \(a_i\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(b_i\in\mathbb R\) for \(1\le i\le m\), and define
\[
f(y)=\max_{1\le i\le m}\{\langle a_i,y\rangle+b_i\},
\qquad (Ay)_i=\langle a_i,y\rangle,
\qquad b=(b_i)_{i=1}^m.
\]
For every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\gamma>0\), choose
\[
\lambda^*\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_{\lambda\in\Delta_m}
\left\{\frac{\gamma}{2}\|A^\mathsf T\lambda\|^2-\langle\lambda,Ax+b\rangle\right\}.
\]
Then
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(x)=x-\gamma A^\mathsf T\lambda^*.
\]
The proximal point is independent of the selected dual minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal map of a finite maximum of affine functions reduces to a convex quadratic optimization problem over the probability simplex, and every dual minimizer yields the same proximal point.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(b_i\in\mathbb R\) for \(1\le i\le m\).

notation.meaning: Probability simplex consisting of nonnegative vectors in R^m whose coordinates sum to one.
Linear map from R^n to R^m whose i-th component is the inner product with a_i.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite maximum represented by maximization over the simplex and reduced by convex duality

children.title: Indexed Supremum Forms

knowledge_statements.title: Indexed Supremum Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measure-valued reduction for a compactly indexed supremum of affine functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U\) be compact, let \(a:U\to\mathbb R^n\) and \(b:U\to\mathbb R\) be continuous, and define \(f(y)=\sup_{u\in U}\{\langle a(u),y\rangle+b(u)\}\). If \(\mathcal P(U)\) is the set of Borel probability measures on \(U\), choose
\[
\mu^*\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_{\mu\in\mathcal P(U)}
\left\{\frac{\gamma}{2}\left\|\int_U a\,d\mu\right\|^2-
\int_U(\langle a(u),x\rangle+b(u))\,d\mu(u)\right\}.
\]
Then \(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(x)=x-\gamma\int_U a\,d\mu^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compactly indexed affine supremum admits a probability-measure dual problem; its optimal averaged slope determines the proximal point.

notation.meaning: An optimal probability measure in the dual reduction.

measure-valued minimax hypotheses require source confirmation

children.title: Simplex Reduction Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Simplex Reduction Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-face conditions for the simplex reduction of maximum-affine proximal maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m\in\mathbb N\) with \(m\ge1\), let \(a_i\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(b_i\in\mathbb R\) for \(1\le i\le m\), and define
\[
f(y)=\max_{1\le i\le m}\{\langle a_i,y\rangle+b_i\},
\qquad (Ay)_i=\langle a_i,y\rangle,
\qquad \Delta_m=\{\lambda\in\mathbb R^m:\lambda_i\ge0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i=1\}.
\]
For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\gamma>0\), let \(\lambda^*\in\Delta_m\) solve the simplex quadratic program associated with the proximal map and set \(p=x-\gamma A^\mathsf T\lambda^*\). Then, for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\),
\[
\lambda_i^*>0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\langle a_i,p\rangle+b_i=f(p),
\]
and
\[
\frac{x-p}{\gamma}=A^\mathsf T\lambda^*\in\partial f(p).
\]
Consequently, the support of \(\lambda^*\) is contained in the set of affine pieces active at \(p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimal simplex weight vector is supported only on affine pieces active at the proximal point, and its weighted slope equals the proximal residual divided by gamma.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(b_i\in\mathbb R\) for \(1\le i\le m\).
\(\lambda^*\) solves the associated simplex quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), \(\lambda_i^*>0\Rightarrow\langle a_i,p\rangle+b_i=f(p)\), and \((x-p)/\gamma=A^\mathsf T\lambda^*\in\partial f(p)\).

notation.meaning: Linear map whose i-th component is the inner product with a_i.

children.title: Dual Supremum Reductions

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Supremum Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moreau reduction for conjugates, including support functions generated by suprema.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex on a real Hilbert space, and let \(f=g^*\). For every \(x\) and \(\gamma>0\), Moreau decomposition gives
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(x)=x-\gamma\operatorname{prox}_{g/\gamma}(x/\gamma).
\]
In particular, if \(f=\sigma_C\) is the support function of a nonempty closed convex set \(C\), then \(f=\delta_C^*\) and
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\sigma_C}(x)=x-\gamma P_C(x/\gamma).
\]
Thus a supremum-defined support function is evaluated proximally through a projection onto its dual generating set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Moreau decomposition converts the proximal map of a conjugate into a dual proximal map; for support functions, this becomes projection onto the generating set.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
For the specialization, \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: scaled Moreau decomposition and the conjugacy between an indicator and a support function

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scaled Moreau identity and support-function specialization are correct and appropriately classified as duality, but no inspectable citation is supplied.

children.title: Scalar Loss Forms

knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Loss Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar optimality equation and coordinatewise lifting for separable losses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\phi:\mathbb R\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. For every \(t\in\mathbb R\) and \(\gamma>0\), the scalar proximal point \(p=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\phi}(t)\) is the unique \(p\in\mathbb R\) satisfying
\[
0\in\partial\phi(p)+\frac{p-t}{\gamma}.
\]
If \(p\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}\phi)\) and \(\phi\) is differentiable at \(p\), then
\[
p+\gamma\phi'(p)=t.
\]
More generally, let \(n\in\mathbb N\) with \(n\ge1\), let each \(\phi_j:\mathbb R\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and define \(F:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) by \(F(x)=\sum_{j=1}^n\phi_j(x_j)\). Then, for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\),
\[
(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma F}(x))_j=
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\phi_j}(x_j)
\qquad(1\le j\le n).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scalar convex loss proximal point satisfies a one-dimensional subdifferential inclusion. For a finite sum of coordinate-separable proper closed convex losses, the proximal map acts coordinate by coordinate.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi:\mathbb R\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
For the separable extension, \(n\ge1\) and each \(\phi_j:\mathbb R\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: scalar proximal optimality and separability of the squared Euclidean norm

children.title: Entropy Forms

knowledge_statements.title: Entropy Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lambert-W formula for the proximal map of scalar Boltzmann–Shannon entropy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(h(t)=t\log t\) for \(t>0\), \(h(0)=0\), and \(h(t)=+\infty\) for \(t<0\). For every \(x\in\mathbb R\) and \(\gamma>0\), the proximal point is positive and is given by
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma h}(x)
=\gamma W_0\!\left(\frac{1}{\gamma}
\exp\!\left(\frac{x}{\gamma}-1\right)\right),
\]
where \(W_0\) is the principal real Lambert function. Equivalently, it is the unique \(p>0\) satisfying \(p+\gamma\log p=x-\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal map of scalar negative entropy is positive and has a closed form through the principal Lambert W function.
assumptions_latex: \(h(t)=t\log t\) on the positive half-line with its closed convex extension at zero.

notation.meaning: Principal real branch of the Lambert W function.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct inversion of the entropy proximal optimality equation using the Lambert W identity

children.title: Domain-Restricted Scalar Forms

knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Restricted Scalar Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clipping rule for a convex scalar function restricted to a closed interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\phi:\mathbb R\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, let \(-\infty<\ell\le u<+\infty\), and suppose \(\operatorname{dom}\phi\) contains \([\ell,u]\). Define \(f=\phi+\delta_{[\ell,u]}\). For every \(x\in\mathbb R\) and \(\gamma>0\),
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(x)
=P_{[\ell,u]}\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\phi}(x)\bigr)
=\min\{u,\max\{\ell,\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\phi}(x)\}\}.
\]
Thus interval restriction clips the unrestricted scalar proximal point to the feasible interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex scalar function restricted to a closed interval, compute the unrestricted proximal point and clip it to the interval.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.

notation.meaning: Metric projection, or clipping, onto the interval.

children.title: Endpoint Activity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Transitions where proximal solutions reach domain boundaries.

knowledge_statements.title: Endpoint Activity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact threshold conditions for interval endpoints to become proximal minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\phi\) be convex and finite on an open interval containing \([\ell,u]\), and minimize \(\phi(p)+(p-x)^2/(2\gamma)\) over \(p\in[\ell,u]\). With one-sided derivatives at the endpoints, the unique minimizer \(p^*\) satisfies
\[
p^*=\ell\iff x\le \ell+\gamma\phi'_+(\ell),
\qquad
p^*=u\iff x\ge u+\gamma\phi'_-(u).
\]
Outside these endpoint regimes, \(p^*\in(\ell,u)\) and
\[
0\in\partial\phi(p^*)+\frac{p^*-x}{\gamma}.
\]
If \(\phi\) is differentiable inside the interval, the last inclusion is \(p^*+\gamma\phi'(p^*)=x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Endpoint activity is determined by one-sided derivative thresholds; between them, the proximal point satisfies the ordinary interior optimality equation.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi\) is convex and finite on an open interval containing \([\ell,u]\).

notation.meaning: Right derivative of phi at the lower endpoint.
Left derivative of phi at the upper endpoint.

knowledge_statements.title: Transcendental Reduction Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar proximal evaluations reduced to monotone transcendental equations, including an exponential example.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\gamma>0\), \(x\in\mathbb{R}\), and let \(\phi:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable and convex. Then \(p=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\phi}(x)\) is the unique solution of \(p+\gamma\phi'(p)=x\). Thus evaluation reduces to inversion of the strictly increasing map \(t\mapsto t+\gamma\phi'(t)\). In particular, for \(\phi(t)=e^t\), the equation \(p+\gamma e^p=x\) gives \[\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma e^{(\cdot)}}(x)=x-W(\gamma e^x),\] where \(W\) is the principal Lambert function satisfying \(W(s)e^{W(s)}=s\) for \(s\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A differentiable scalar proximal problem reduces to a monotone equation; for the exponential function, its solution is expressed using the principal Lambert W function.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean projection onto a nonempty affine solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), let \(b\in\operatorname{ran}A\), and define \(C=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^n:Az=b\}\). For every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the Euclidean projection onto \(C\) is \[P_C(x)=x-A^{\dagger}(Ax-b),\] where \(A^{\dagger}\) is the Moore--Penrose pseudoinverse. Equivalently, \(P_C(x)\) is the unique point \(p\in C\) such that \(x-p\in(\ker A)^{\perp}=\operatorname{ran}A^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection onto a consistent affine system subtracts the pseudoinverse correction and leaves a residual orthogonal to the affine direction space.
assumptions_latex: \(C=\{z:Az=b\}\) and projection uses the Euclidean norm.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT certificate for Euclidean projection onto a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^n:Az\leq b,\;Ez=d\}\) be nonempty. A point \(p\) equals \(P_C(x)\) if and only if there exist multipliers \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\) and \(\nu\in\mathbb{R}^q\) such that \[Ap\leq b,\qquad Ep=d,\qquad p-x+A^{\mathsf T}\lambda+E^{\mathsf T}\nu=0,\qquad \lambda_i((Ap)_i-b_i)=0\ \text{for every }i.\] These conditions certify global optimality because \(p\) minimizes the strongly convex quadratic \(z\mapsto\tfrac12\|z-x\|_2^2\) over \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection onto a polyhedron is certified by primal feasibility, nonnegative inequality multipliers, stationarity, and complementary slackness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=P_C(x)\) if and only if the displayed primal-dual conditions hold.

children.title: Order-Constrained Sets

knowledge_statements.title: Order-Constrained Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean projection onto the monotone cone by isotonic regression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^n:z_1\leq\cdots\leq z_n\}\). For \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), its projection \(p=P_C(x)\) is the unique isotonic least-squares solution. Its coordinates admit the min--max representation \[p_i=\max_{1\leq a\leq i}\ \min_{i\leq b\leq n}\frac{1}{b-a+1}\sum_{j=a}^{b}x_j,\qquad i=1,\ldots,n.\] Equivalently, the pool-adjacent-violators procedure repeatedly merges neighboring blocks whose current means violate nondecreasing order and assigns each final block its mean.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection onto the nondecreasing cone is isotonic regression, computable by pooling adjacent violating blocks and assigning their means.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_C(x)\) has the displayed coordinatewise min--max representation.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(r>0\) and define \(\Delta_r=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^n:z_i\geq0,\ \sum_{i=1}^n z_i=r\}\). For every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), there is a unique scalar \(\tau\in\mathbb{R}\) satisfying \[\sum_{i=1}^n\max\{x_i-\tau,0\}=r.\] The Euclidean projection is then \[(P_{\Delta_r}(x))_i=\max\{x_i-\tau,0\},\qquad i=1,\ldots,n.\] The threshold may be found after sorting the coordinates of \(x\), or by monotone scalar root finding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simplex projection shifts every coordinate by one common threshold, truncates at zero, and chooses the threshold to preserve the required sum.

knowledge_statements.title: Box Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise Euclidean projection onto a closed axis-aligned box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\ell,u\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy \(\ell_i\leq u_i\) for every \(i\), and define \(B=[\ell,u]=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^n:\ell_i\leq z_i\leq u_i\}\). The squared Euclidean distance to \(x\) separates by coordinate, so the unique projection is \[(P_B(x))_i=\min\{u_i,\max\{\ell_i,x_i\}\},\qquad i=1,\ldots,n.\] Thus coordinates below, inside, and above their intervals are respectively raised to \(\ell_i\), unchanged, and lowered to \(u_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection onto a box clips each coordinate independently to its lower and upper bounds.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unit Box in Euclidean Space
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the closed unit box as a coordinatewise interval set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(n\in\mathbb N\), the \(n\)-dimensional unit box is
\[
B_n:=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:0\le x^{(i)}\le 1,\ i=1,\ldots,n\}=[0,1]^n.
\]

children.title: Norm Balls
children.top_down_role: Projection families for sets bounded by norm radii.

knowledge_statements.title: Norm Balls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection onto a norm ball through the proximal mapping of the dual norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\|\cdot\|\) be a norm on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(\|\cdot\|_*\) be its dual norm, and set \(B_r=\{z:\|z\|\leq r\}\) for \(r>0\). Since the support function of \(B_r\) is \(\sigma_{B_r}(y)=r\|y\|_*\), Moreau decomposition yields \[P_{B_r}(x)=\operatorname{prox}_{\delta_{B_r}}(x)=x-\operatorname{prox}_{r\|\cdot\|_*}(x).\] In the Euclidean case this becomes \(P_{B_r}(x)=x\min\{1,r/\|x\|_2\}\), with the value at \(x=0\) understood as \(0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection onto any norm ball is complementary to the proximal map of the scaled dual norm; Euclidean balls reduce to radial scaling.
assumptions_latex: \(\|\cdot\|\) is a norm on \(\mathbb{R}^n\) with dual norm \(\|\cdot\|_*\).

notation.meaning: Closed radius-r ball of the given norm.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty closed convex cone and define its polar cone by \(K^\circ=\{y:\langle y,z\rangle\leq0\ \text{for every }z\in K\}\). Every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) has the orthogonal decomposition \[x=P_K(x)+P_{K^\circ}(x),\qquad \langle P_K(x),P_{K^\circ}(x)\rangle=0.\] Consequently, either projection determines the other: \(P_K(x)=x-P_{K^\circ}(x)\). Closedness of \(K\) ensures that projection onto \(K\) is attained for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every vector splits uniquely into orthogonal projections onto a closed convex cone and its polar cone.

children.title: Gauge Balls
children.top_down_role: Projection families induced by sublevel sets of gauges.

knowledge_statements.title: Gauge Balls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gauge sublevel sets and their projection-support-function relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, convex, and contain \(0\), and define its gauge by \(\gamma_C(x)=\inf\{t\geq0:x\in tC\}\). Then \[C=\{x:\gamma_C(x)\leq1\}.\] Moreover, because the conjugate of the indicator \(\delta_C\) is the support function \(\sigma_C\), Moreau decomposition gives \[P_C(x)=\operatorname{prox}_{\delta_C}(x)=x-\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma_C}(x).\] Hence projection onto a closed gauge ball is reducible to proximal evaluation of its support function, without requiring symmetry of \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex set containing zero is its gauge unit ball, and its projection is complementary to the proximal map of its support function.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, closed, convex, and contains \(0\).

children.title: Polar-Set Relations
children.top_down_role: Links between projections onto gauge sets and their polar counterparts.

knowledge_statements.title: Polar-Set Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gauge-support duality for a closed convex set containing the origin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed and convex with \(0\in C\), and define its polar set by \[C^\circ=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle y,x\rangle\leq1\ \text{for every }x\in C\}.\] Then the bipolar identity and gauge-support identities are \[C^{\circ\circ}=C,\qquad \gamma_C(x)=\sigma_{C^\circ}(x),\qquad \gamma_{C^\circ}(y)=\sigma_C(y).\] These equalities remain valid for extended-valued gauges when \(C\) is not absorbing or is unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polarity is involutive on closed convex sets containing zero, and each set's gauge equals the support function of its polar.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bipolar and gauge-support identities are correct for a closed convex set containing the origin, with extended-valued gauges allowed. The cited section on convex and affine hulls does not specifically support polarity, bipolarity, or gauge-support duality.

children.title: Nonclosed Set Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Projection limitations for nonclosed or otherwise ill-posed geometric sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonclosed Set Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of projection attainment when the target set is not closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Closedness cannot be omitted from the general projection-existence statement. In \(\mathbb{R}\), let \(C=(0,\infty)\) and \(x=0\). Then \[\inf_{z\in C}|x-z|=0,\] but no \(p\in C\) attains this infimum. Accordingly, \(P_C(0)\) is empty and the minimization defining \(\operatorname{prox}_{\delta_C}(0)\) has no solution. The closure has projection \(P_{\overline C}(0)=0\), showing that replacing a nonclosed set by its closure changes attainment at excluded boundary points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonclosed convex set may have no nearest point: zero has distance zero from the positive open ray, but no projection onto it.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convexity of Sublevel Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to every real sublevel of a convex function on a convex domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex and let \(g:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex. Then, for every \(c\in\mathbb{R}\), the sublevel set \(\Gamma_c=\{x\in\Omega:g(x)\le c\}\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every sublevel set of a convex function on a convex domain is convex.

children.title: Convex Sublevel Sets
children.top_down_role: Projection onto level-bounded regions induced by convex functions.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Sublevel Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection onto a convex sublevel set through a scalar proximal multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and let \(S_\alpha=\{z:f(z)\leq\alpha\}\). Assume there exists \(z_0\) with \(f(z_0)<\alpha\). If \(x\notin S_\alpha\), then there is a multiplier \(\lambda>0\) such that \[P_{S_\alpha}(x)=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x),\qquad f(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x))=\alpha.\] If \(x\in S_\alpha\), then \(P_{S_\alpha}(x)=x\). Thus the exterior projection reduces to finding a scalar multiplier enforcing the active level constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection onto a convex sublevel set is trivial inside; outside, it is a scaled proximal point whose function value reaches the boundary level.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.

notation.meaning: Closed convex alpha-sublevel set of f.
Lagrange multiplier for the active level constraint.

children.title: Convex Epigraph Sets
children.top_down_role: Projection onto lifted sets above convex function graphs.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Epigraph Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph characterization for extended-real-valued convex functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a real vector space \(X\) and a function \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), its epigraph is \[\operatorname{epi}f=\{(x,t)\in X\times\mathbb R:f(x)\le t\}.\] The function \(f\) is convex if and only if \(\operatorname{epi}f\) is a convex subset of \(X\times\mathbb R\). If \(X\) is finite-dimensional, then \(f\) is lower semicontinuous if and only if \(\operatorname{epi}f\) is closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The epigraph contains every point lying on or above the graph. Its convexity characterizes convex functions, and its closedness characterizes lower semicontinuity in finite dimensions.
assumptions_latex: X\text{ is a real vector space}

children.title: Level-Parameter Regimes
children.top_down_role: Changes in sublevel-set geometry as the level parameter varies.

knowledge_statements.title: Level-Parameter Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification of sublevel sets relative to a finite infimum and its attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a real vector space, let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), suppose \(m=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\in\mathbb R\), and, for each \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\), define \(L_\alpha=\{x\in X:f(x)\le\alpha\}\). Then \(L_\alpha=\varnothing\) when \(\alpha<m\), \(L_\alpha\ne\varnothing\) when \(\alpha>m\), and \(L_m\ne\varnothing\) if and only if the infimum is attained. For all \(\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb R\), \(\alpha\le\beta\) implies \(L_\alpha\subseteq L_\beta\), and \[L_\alpha=\{x\in X:(x,\alpha)\in\operatorname{epi}f\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a function with finite infimum, sublevel sets are empty below the infimum, nonempty above it, and nonempty at the infimum exactly when a minimizer exists. They are nested as the real-valued level increases and equal fixed-height slices of the epigraph.
assumptions_latex: X\text{ is a real vector space}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha<m\Rightarrow L_\alpha=\varnothing,\quad \alpha>m\Rightarrow L_\alpha\ne\varnothing,\quad L_m\ne\varnothing\iff m\text{ is attained}

notation.meaning: sublevel set of f at the real level alpha
finite infimum of f over X

children.title: Epigraph Lifting Relations
children.top_down_role: Connections between function representations and lifted projection geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Epigraph Lifting Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sublevel constraints represented by one-dimensional epigraph lifting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\), the constraint \(f(x)\le\alpha\) has the lifted representation \[x\in L_\alpha\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (x,\alpha)\in\operatorname{epi}f.\] More generally, for a set \(C\subseteq X\), \[\{x\in C:f(x)\le\alpha\}=\operatorname{proj}_X\bigl((C\times\{\alpha\})\cap\operatorname{epi}f\bigr).\] Thus a convex inequality becomes membership in a convex lifted set whenever \(C\) and \(f\) are convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sublevel constraint is exactly a fixed-height slice of the epigraph; adding other constraints corresponds to intersecting in the lifted space and projecting back.

children.title: Spectral Proximal Forms
children.top_down_role: Matrix proximal mappings reducible to eigenvalue or singular-value operations.

children.title: Symmetric Eigenvalue Forms
children.top_down_role: Orthogonally invariant symmetric-matrix proximal families.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric Eigenvalue Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean proximal reduction for convex orthogonally invariant functions on symmetric matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and invariant under coordinate permutations, and set \(F(X)=\phi(\lambda(X))\) on \(\mathbb S^n\). If \(X=Q\operatorname{Diag}(\lambda)Q^{\mathsf T}\), then for every \(\gamma>0\), \[\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma F}(X)=Q\operatorname{Diag}\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\phi}(\lambda)\bigr)Q^{\mathsf T}.\] The vector proximal point respects equal-eigenvalue blocks, so the resulting matrix is independent of the chosen eigendecomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal map of a convex symmetric eigenvalue function preserves eigenvectors and applies the corresponding vector proximal map to the eigenvalues.

notation.meaning: eigenvalue vector of X in a fixed order

children.title: Singular-Value Forms
children.top_down_role: Unitarily invariant rectangular-matrix proximal families.

knowledge_statements.title: Singular-Value Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean proximal reduction for convex unitarily invariant rectangular-matrix functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r=\min\{m,n\}\), let \(\phi:\mathbb R^r\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and absolutely symmetric, and set \(F(X)=\phi(\sigma(X))\). For a singular-value decomposition \(X=U\operatorname{Diag}(\sigma)V^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\gamma>0\), \[\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma F}(X)=U\operatorname{Diag}\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\phi}(\sigma)\bigr)V^{\mathsf T},\] with compatible zero padding in a full rectangular decomposition. The value is independent of the selected singular vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal map of a convex singular-value function preserves singular vectors and applies the corresponding absolutely symmetric vector proximal map to singular values.

children.title: Spectral Constraint Projections

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Constraint Projections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection reduction for convex eigenvalue and singular-value constraint sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, convex, and permutation invariant. For \(C=\{X\in\mathbb S^n:\lambda(X)\in D\}\) and \(X=Q\operatorname{Diag}(\lambda)Q^{\mathsf T}\), \[P_C(X)=Q\operatorname{Diag}(P_D(\lambda))Q^{\mathsf T}.\] Likewise, if \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^r\) is nonempty, closed, convex, and absolutely symmetric, then projection onto \(C_\sigma=\{X:\sigma(X)\in D\}\) is obtained by retaining the singular vectors and replacing \(\sigma(X)\) by \(P_D(\sigma(X))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection onto an invariant spectral constraint set reduces to Euclidean projection of the eigenvalue or singular-value vector onto its defining vector set.

X\text{ is a compatible real matrix}

children.title: Proximal Recognition-Validation Interface

children.title: Canonical-Form Normalization
children.top_down_role: Rewriting terms into recognized proximal families.

knowledge_statements.title: Canonical-Form Normalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalization of translated, tilted, and positively scaled proximal terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(g(x)=a f(x-b)+\langle c,x\rangle+d\), a query \(x\), and \(\gamma>0\), where \(a>0\) and a catalog formula for \(\operatorname{prox}_{\tau f}\) is available. Set \(y=x-b-\gamma c\) and \(\tau=\gamma a\); evaluate \(z=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau f}(y)\); output \(b+z\). Then \[\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma g}(x)=b+\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma a f}(x-b-\gamma c).\] The additive constant \(d\) is discarded. Evaluation terminates after the catalog proximal call.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalize a translated, linearly tilted, positively scaled function by shifting the query, scaling the proximal parameter, ignoring constants, and invoking the base proximal formula.

notation.meaning: proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions on H
normalized proximal parameter gamma times a

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normalization algorithm and transformation formula are mathematically correct and appropriately classified, but no source or inspectable locator supports the nontrivial proximal transformation rule.

children.title: Proximal Compatibility Matching
children.top_down_role: Compatibility checks for cataloged proximal forms.

children.title: Proximal Parameter Matching
children.top_down_role: Alignment of catalog entries with proximal scale conventions.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Parameter Matching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact matching of catalog and query proximal scaling conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the query defines \[p=\arg\min_u\left\{a f(u)+\frac{b}{2}\lVert u-x\rVert^2\right\},\] where \(a>0\) and \(b>0\), while the catalog convention is \(\operatorname{prox}_{\tau f}(x)=\arg\min_u\{\tau f(u)+\tfrac12\lVert u-x\rVert^2\}\). Parameter compatibility holds exactly when \(\tau=a/b\); under this condition, \(p=\operatorname{prox}_{(a/b)f}(x)\). In the equivalent convention using \(f(u)+\lVert u-x\rVert^2/(2\gamma)\), the matching parameter is \(\gamma=a/b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Match the proximal parameter by dividing the coefficient of the function by the quadratic coefficient after normalizing the quadratic term to one half.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coefficient normalization and parameter conversion are correct and fit the matching-condition leaf, but the record provides no supporting source with a locator.

children.title: Metric Matching
children.top_down_role: Alignment of evaluation forms with Euclidean or variable-metric geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Metric Matching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility between a variable-metric proximal query and a Euclidean catalog formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be bounded, self-adjoint, and strongly positive on a real Hilbert space, and define \[\operatorname{prox}^{M}_{\gamma f}(x)=\arg\min_u\left\{\gamma f(u)+\frac12\langle M(u-x),u-x\rangle\right\}.\] A Euclidean catalog formula applies directly only when \(M=I\). More generally, with \(T=M^{1/2}\), metric matching by change of variables gives \[\operatorname{prox}^{M}_{\gamma f}(x)=T^{-1}\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma(f\circ T^{-1})}(Tx).\] Thus the transformed function must itself match the catalog family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable-metric proximal problem matches a Euclidean formula directly only for the identity metric, or after a square-root coordinate change that preserves the catalog family.

notation.meaning: proximal map in the M-induced metric

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The square-root change-of-variables identity is correct under the stated strong-positivity assumptions, but this nontrivial variable-metric formula has no cited source.

children.title: Effective-Domain Matching
children.top_down_role: Compatibility between catalog assumptions and function domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Effective-Domain Matching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain compatibility required when recognizing a transformed proximal family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f,g:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and suppose recognition proposes \(g(x)=a f(Tx+b)+\ell(x)+d\), where \(a>0\), \(T\) is linear, and \(\ell\) is finite affine. The proposed family is domain-compatible exactly when \[\operatorname{dom}g=\{x\in H:Tx+b\in\operatorname{dom}f\}=T^{-1}(\operatorname{dom}f-b).\] Any additional indicator constraint must therefore appear in this preimage. Equality only on finite-valued interiors is insufficient when boundary or infeasible query points can affect the proximal minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transformed term matches a catalog family only when its complete effective domain equals the affine preimage of the catalog function’s domain, including boundary constraints.

notation.meaning: preimage of a set S under T

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The effective-domain identity is correct when the proposed global functional representation holds and fits the domain-matching leaf. No authoritative source or inspectable locator is supplied.

children.title: Convention Mismatch Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Recognition failures caused by incompatible scaling, metrics, or domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Convention Mismatch Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure caused by confusing reciprocal proximal-parameter conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(u)=u^2/2\) on \(\mathbb R\) and let \(\gamma>0\). Under the convention \[P_\gamma(x)=\arg\min_u\left\{\gamma f(u)+\frac12(u-x)^2\right\},\] one has \(P_\gamma(x)=x/(1+\gamma)\). Under \[Q_\gamma(x)=\arg\min_u\left\{f(u)+\frac{\gamma}{2}(u-x)^2\right\},\] one has \(Q_\gamma(x)=\gamma x/(1+\gamma)\). Hence identically named parameters cannot be transferred between these conventions: for \(x\ne0\), the results agree only when \(\gamma=1\); the correct conversion is \(Q_\gamma=P_{1/\gamma}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two common quadratic-weight conventions produce different proximal points for the same numeric parameter; they agree generally only after replacing the parameter by its reciprocal.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quadratic counterexample, disagreement boundary, and reciprocal conversion are correct and appropriately classified as a failure boundary, but the record lacks source support.

children.title: Proximal Evaluation-Path Taxonomy

children.title: Closed-Form Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Direct proximal evaluation through cataloged explicit forms.

knowledge_statements.title: Closed-Form Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct evaluation when the proximal optimality inclusion has an explicit resolvent formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(f\in\Gamma_0(H)\), \(x\in H\), and \(\gamma>0\), together with a validated explicit single-valued expression \(R_\gamma\) satisfying \[x-R_\gamma(x)\in\gamma\,\partial f(R_\gamma(x)).\] Evaluate \(p=R_\gamma(x)\), verify the expression's parameter, metric, and domain conditions, and output \(p\). Then \[p=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(x)=(I+\gamma\partial f)^{-1}(x).\] Evaluation is closed-form when computing \(R_\gamma(x)\) requires only a fixed finite composition of specified elementary operations, without iterative optimization or root solving.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate a validated explicit resolvent expression, check its parameter, metric, and domain conditions, and return it as the proximal point without an iterative solve.
assumptions_latex: R_\gamma\text{ satisfies the displayed inclusion for every admissible }x

children.title: Structured Linear Solves
children.top_down_role: Proximal evaluation reduced to structured linear algebra.

knowledge_statements.title: Structured Linear Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex quadratic proximal evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(v\), form \(M=I+\gamma Q\) and \(b=v-\gamma c\). Compute the unique solution \(p\) of \[Mp=b.\] Return \(p\) as \(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(v)\). An exact factorization, sparse direct solve, or structure-preserving iterative method may be used, provided it returns the solution of this system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate the proximal mapping of the convex quadratic by solving its positive-definite structured linear system.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space.
\(Q:H\to H\) is self-adjoint and positive semidefinite, \(c,v\in H\), and \(\gamma>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(v)\) is the unique solution of \((I+\gamma Q)p=v-\gamma c\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: first-order optimality for a convex quadratic proximal subproblem yields a positive-definite structured linear system

children.title: Scalar Root Solves
children.top_down_role: Proximal evaluation reduced to a one-dimensional implicit problem.

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space and \(v\in H\).
\(\phi:[0,\infty)\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, convex, nondecreasing, and differentiable on \((0,\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The proximal evaluation reduces to a unique one-dimensional convex minimization, and to a scalar root when its minimizer is positive.

notation.meaning: Proximal mapping of the radial function

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: radial symmetry reduces the proximal problem to a strongly convex scalar problem
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Radial convex functions with a differentiable scalar profile.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(s=\lVert v\rVert\). If \(s=0\), return \(0\). Otherwise compute the unique minimizer \[r_\star=\operatorname*{argmin}_{r\geq 0}\left\{\phi(r)+\frac{(r-s)^2}{2\gamma}\right\}.\] When \(r_\star>0\), it is the unique root on \((0,\infty)\) of \[F(r)=\phi'(r)+\gamma^{-1}(r-s)=0.\] When the right derivative satisfies \(F(0+)\geq 0\), take \(r_\star=0\). Return \[\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(v)=\frac{r_\star}{s}v.\] A bracketing root solver preserves the scalar-domain constraint \(r\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex radial function, proximal evaluation preserves direction and determines the radius by a unique scalar convex problem or root equation.
knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Root Solves

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The radial reduction, boundary case, and scalar root characterization are mathematically coherent and the algorithm kind fits the leaf. No citation with an inspectable locator supports the reduction or its hypotheses.

children.title: Evaluation-Path Selection
children.top_down_role: Structural criteria for choosing among available evaluation regimes.

assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex on a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space.
\(v\in H\), \(\gamma>0\), and every selected computation is validated against the proximal optimality inclusion.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \((f,v,\gamma)\), select the first applicable validated path in the following order: use a recognized closed formula; otherwise reduce quadratic or affine optimality equations to a structured linear solve; otherwise use a proved scalar parameterization and solve its monotone scalar equation; otherwise solve the strongly convex proximal subproblem numerically. children.title: Closed-Form Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases requiring an inner solve despite superficial resemblance to cataloged forms.

knowledge_statements.title: Closed-Form Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of coordinatewise formulas under quadratic coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=\begin{pmatrix}1&\rho\\rho&1\end{pmatrix}\), \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx\), and \(v=(1,0)^{\mathsf T}\). Then \[\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(v)=\frac{1}{(1+\gamma)^2-\gamma^2\rho^2}\begin{pmatrix}1+\gamma\\-\gamma\rho\end{pmatrix}.\] Since \(0<|\rho|<1\), its second coordinate is nonzero. Applying the one-dimensional quadratic proximal formula independently to the two coordinates would instead return a zero second coordinate and therefore does not evaluate this coupled proximal mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An off-diagonal positive-definite quadratic provides a counterexample to coordinatewise application of scalar proximal formulas.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coupled mapping \(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}\) cannot be evaluated by applying the scalar quadratic proximal formula independently to the coordinates.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: an off-diagonal positive-definite quadratic explicitly defeats coordinatewise proximal evaluation

children.title: Proximal Oracle Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Exact or approximate oracle contracts and computed-point validation.

children.title: Exact Proximal Oracles
children.top_down_role: Interfaces returning exact proximal evaluations.

assumptions_latex: \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex on a real Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An exact oracle returns the unique \(p\) satisfying \(0\in\partial f(p)+\gamma^{-1}(p-v)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the exact proximal oracle is defined by the unique minimizer and its equivalent subdifferential inclusion
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact oracle for proper closed convex functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exact proximal oracle for \(f\) is a mapping \(\mathcal O_f:H\times(0,\infty)\to H\) such that, for every query \((v,\gamma)\), its output \(p=\mathcal O_f(v,\gamma)\) satisfies \[p=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in H}\left\{f(x)+\frac{1}{2\gamma}\lVert x-v\rVert^2\right\}.\] Equivalently, the output satisfies \[0\in\partial f(p)+\gamma^{-1}(p-v),\qquad\text{or}\qquad \frac{v-p}{\gamma}\in\partial f(p).\] Strong convexity of the proximal objective makes this output unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact proximal oracle returns the unique minimizer of the regularized objective, equivalently the unique point satisfying the proximal subgradient inclusion.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Proximal Oracles

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically correct, introduces its objects, and fits Exact Proximal Oracles, but no inspectable source is cited.

children.title: Approximate Proximal Oracles
children.top_down_role: Interfaces returning controlled inexact proximal evaluations.

assumptions_latex: \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex on a real Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A residual-certified approximate oracle returns \((p,u)\) with \(u\in\partial f(p)\) and \(\lVert p+\gamma u-v\rVert\leq\varepsilon\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a computable norm bound on the proximal inclusion residual defines a standard approximate oracle model
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute residual model for approximate proximal evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A residual-certified \(\varepsilon\)-approximate proximal oracle for \(f\) maps a query \((v,\gamma,\varepsilon)\) to a pair \((p,u)\) satisfying \[p\in\operatorname{dom}f,\qquad u\in\partial f(p),\qquad \lVert p+\gamma u-v\rVert\leq\varepsilon.\] The oracle must return the witness \(u\), or equivalent data from which membership \(u\in\partial f(p)\) and the residual can be checked. At \(\varepsilon=0\), this definition reduces to the exact proximal oracle condition. The tolerance is absolute in the primal-space norm and must accompany the output.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate proximal oracle supplies a feasible point and subgradient witness whose proximal optimality residual is no larger than the declared absolute tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Proximal Oracles

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a coherent absolute residual oracle definition and is explicit about its witness and norm, but approximate-proximal conventions vary. The selected convention requires a cited source with a specific locator.

children.title: Optimality-Residual Validation
children.top_down_role: Residual-based checks for computed proximal points.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimality-Residual Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori validation using a subgradient witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proposed point \(p\) and certified witness \(u\in\partial f(p)\), form \[r=p+\gamma u-v.\] The residual supplies the error certificate \[\left\lVert p-\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(v)\right\rVert\leq\lVert r\rVert.\] Thus \(\lVert r\rVert\leq\varepsilon\) certifies distance at most \(\varepsilon\) from the exact proximal point, while \(r=0\) certifies exactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified subgradient witness makes the proximal inclusion residual an upper bound on the distance to the exact proximal point.
assumptions_latex: \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex on a real Hilbert space.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: resolvent nonexpansiveness converts the proximal inclusion residual into a pointwise error certificate

children.title: Domain-Feasibility Validation
children.top_down_role: Checks that computed points respect effective-domain restrictions.

assumptions_latex: \(p\in H\) is a proposed proximal output.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Domain feasibility is certified by finite evaluation \(f(p)<+\infty\), while a subgradient certificate additionally requires a verifiable \(u\in\partial f(p)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite objective value is precisely effective-domain membership, and subgradient membership supplies a stronger local feasibility witness
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effective-domain and subgradient-witness checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A proposed output \(p\) passes domain-feasibility validation precisely when \[f(p)<+\infty,\] equivalently \(p\in\operatorname{dom}f\). If the oracle also claims an optimality-residual certificate using \(u\), validation must establish \[f(z)\geq f(p)+\langle u,z-p\rangle\qquad\text{for every }z\in H,\] or invoke an equivalent certified characterization of \(u\in\partial f(p)\). Failure of finite evaluation invalidates \(p\) as a proximal point. Domain feasibility alone does not establish proximal optimality; it only certifies that the returned point is admissible for the extended-valued objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A candidate is domain-feasible exactly when its objective value is finite; this check is necessary but does not by itself certify proximal optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Feasibility Validation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The domain-feasibility certificate is correct, clearly distinguished from optimality, and appropriate for the leaf. It lacks an inspectable citation.

children.title: Oracle Failure Signals
children.top_down_role: Diagnostic outcomes indicating incompatible inputs or unreliable computed points.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle Failure Signals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Detectable failures in certified proximal evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A claimed exact or \(\varepsilon\)-approximate proximal result fails certification if \(p\notin\operatorname{dom}f\), if a required witness does not satisfy \(u\in\partial f(p)\), or if \[\lVert p+\gamma u-v\rVert>\varepsilon.\] Certification also fails when a hypothesis required by the selected closed formula, linear solve, or scalar reduction cannot be verified. In a numerical implementation, nonfinite reported coordinates or scalar diagnostics are additional implementation-level failure signals. A failed call must not be represented as a certified proximal output.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal-oracle result is uncertified when domain membership, witness validity, residual tolerance, or a required evaluation-path hypothesis fails; numerical implementations must also reject nonfinite reported data.
assumptions_latex: \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex on a real Hilbert space.
\((p,u)\) is a claimed residual-certified output whenever a subgradient witness is required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Violation of any required feasibility, witness, residual, or evaluation-path predicate is an oracle failure signal rather than a certified proximal result.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: certification fails when any required domain, witness, residual, or representation predicate is false

children.title: Subdifferential Optimality Inclusions

children.title: Fermat Optimality Family
children.top_down_role: Unconstrained convex optimality through subdifferential zeros.

knowledge_statements.title: Fermat Optimality Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained convex Fermat rule in a Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the unconstrained convex problem \[\inf_{x\in H}f(x),\] a point \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) is a global minimizer if and only if \[\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in H}f(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in\partial f(\bar x).\] Equivalently, optimal points are precisely the solutions of the inclusion \[0\in\partial f(x).\] No differentiability, strict convexity, or uniqueness is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point globally minimizes a proper convex function exactly when zero belongs to its convex subdifferential.
assumptions_latex: \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and convex on a real Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in H}f(x)\) if and only if \(0\in\partial f(\bar x)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: zero-subgradient optimality is necessary and sufficient for unconstrained convex minimization

children.title: Composite Subdifferential Inclusions
children.top_down_role: Smooth-plus-nonsmooth and linearly composed convex models.

assumptions_latex: \(H\) and \(G\) are finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces, and \(L:H\to G\) is linear.
\(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:G\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper, closed, and convex; \(h:H\to\mathbb R\) is convex and differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A point \(\bar x\) minimizes \(f+h+g\circ L\) if and only if \(0\in\partial f(\bar x)+\nabla h(\bar x)+L^*\partial g(L\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: Linear composition operator and its adjoint

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Fermat's rule combined with differentiable-sum and qualified linear-chain subdifferential calculus gives the inclusion
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth-plus-nonsmooth linear-composite model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(F(x)=f(x)+h(x)+g(Lx)\). Under the stated relative-interior qualification, the subdifferential calculus identity \[\partial F(x)=\partial f(x)+\nabla h(x)+L^*\partial g(Lx)\] holds at every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) with \(Lx\in\operatorname{dom}g\). Consequently, \(\bar x\) solves \(\min_{x\in H}F(x)\) if and only if there exists \(y\in\partial g(L\bar x)\) such that \[0\in\partial f(\bar x)+\nabla h(\bar x)+L^*y.\] This expresses composite convex optimality as a subdifferential inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a relative-interior qualification, minimizing a smooth-plus-nonsmooth linearly composed objective is equivalent to a subdifferential inclusion involving the adjoint operator.
knowledge_statements.title: Composite Subdifferential Inclusions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-dimensional qualification is sufficient for the stated sum and linear-chain calculus, the representation kind matches the leaf, and the conclusion is not overstated. No supporting convex-analysis citation with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Sum-of-Subdifferentials Inclusions
children.top_down_role: Multi-term convex models and their calculus qualifications.

knowledge_statements.title: Sum-of-Subdifferentials Inclusions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite convex sums under a relative-interior qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i\). Under the stated relative-interior qualification, \[\partial F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m\partial f_i(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in\bigcap_{i=1}^m\operatorname{dom}f_i.\] Consequently, \[\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in H}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in\sum_{i=1}^m\partial f_i(\bar x).\] Equivalently, optimality holds exactly when there exist \(u_i\in\partial f_i(\bar x)\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\) such that \(\sum_{i=1}^m u_i=0\). Without a suitable qualification, equality in the subdifferential sum rule is not asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a relative-interior qualification, a point minimizes a finite sum of convex functions exactly when component subgradients can be chosen to sum to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space and \(m\in\mathbb N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\) minimizes \(\sum_{i=1}^m f_i\) if and only if \(0\in\sum_{i=1}^m\partial f_i(\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: Minkowski sum of the component subdifferential sets at the candidate point

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the finite-dimensional relative-interior qualification ensures the exact finite-sum subdifferential rule

children.title: Normal-Cone Inclusion Family
children.top_down_role: Constrained optimality, feasibility, and variational inequalities represented through normal cones.

children.title: Constrained Convex Optimality
children.top_down_role: Objective subdifferentials combined with feasible-set normal cones.

knowledge_statements.title: Constrained Convex Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex Fermat rule with an explicit qualification for the subdifferential sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and let \(C\subset H\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. Assume \(\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\cap\operatorname{ri}C\neq\varnothing\). For \(x\in C\), define \(N_C(x)=\{u\in H:\langle u,y-x\rangle\leq0\ \forall y\in C\}\). Then
\[x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in C}f(y)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in\partial f(x)+N_C(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point minimizes a convex objective exactly when the negative of one objective subgradient is a normal to the feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex; \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.

notation.meaning: convex-analytic normal-cone operator of the feasible set

children.title: Variational-Inequality Inclusions
children.top_down_role: Monotone fields combined with normal-cone operators.

knowledge_statements.title: Variational-Inequality Inclusions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stampacchia variational inequality represented by a normal-cone inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(C\subset H\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(F:C\to H\). With \(N_C(x)=\{u\in H:\langle u,y-x\rangle\leq0\ \forall y\in C\}\) for \(x\in C\), a point \(x\) solves the variational inequality precisely when
\[x\in C,\quad \langle F(x),y-x\rangle\geq0\quad\forall y\in C\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in F(x)+N_C(x).\]
Monotonicity of \(F\) is not needed for this equivalence, but places the resulting sum within monotone inclusion theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variational inequality over a closed convex set is exactly the zero problem for the field plus the set's normal-cone operator.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset H\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.

notation.meaning: normal-cone operator of the constraint set

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct equivalence follows from the standard normal-cone definition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normal-cone equivalence is precise and mathematically standard, but no inspectable source and locator are supplied.

children.title: Convex Feasibility Inclusions
children.top_down_role: Feasibility and best-approximation models expressed through normal operators.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Feasibility Inclusions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intersection feasibility and best approximation expressed as normal-cone zero problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\) be nonempty closed convex subsets of a Hilbert space \(H\). Because \(\operatorname{dom}N_{C_i}=C_i\),
\[x\in\bigcap_{i=1}^m C_i\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in\sum_{i=1}^m N_{C_i}(x).\]
For any nonempty closed convex set \(C\subset H\) and \(z\in H\), the best approximation is characterized by
\[x=P_Cz\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in x-z+N_C(x).\]
Thus feasibility is a normal-cone inclusion, while projection adds the strongly monotone displacement \(x\mapsto x-z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Membership in every convex set is a zero of summed normal cones; projection is a zero of displacement plus the target set's normal cone.
assumptions_latex: \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\) and \(C\) are nonempty, closed, and convex.

notation.meaning: normal-cone operator of a closed convex set

children.title: Monotone Sum Inclusions
children.top_down_role: Operator-sum geometries distinguished by available forward and resolvent access.

children.title: Maximal-Monotone Plus Cocoercive Inclusions
children.top_down_role: The forward–backward-compatible inclusion class.

knowledge_statements.title: Maximal-Monotone Plus Cocoercive Inclusions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward–backward inclusion and its resolvent fixed-point representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space, let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximally monotone, and let \(B:H\to H\) be \(\beta\)-cocoercive for some \(\beta>0\), meaning \(\langle Bx-By,x-y\rangle\geq\beta\|Bx-By\|^2\). For every \(\gamma>0\),
\[0\in Ax+Bx\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x=J_{\gamma A}(x-\gamma Bx),\qquad J_{\gamma A}=(I+\gamma A)^{-1}.\]
When \(0<\gamma<2\beta\), the forward–backward mapping \(J_{\gamma A}(I-\gamma B)\) is averaged, providing the standard fixed-point geometry for this inclusion class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A maximal-monotone plus cocoercive zero is a fixed point of one forward evaluation followed by the maximal operator's resolvent.

source_refs.locator: 10.4 Analysis of the Proximal Gradient Method-The Convex Case p. 281

source_witnesses.locator: 10.4 Analysis of the Proximal Gradient Method-The Convex Case p. 281

children.title: Two Maximally Monotone Operators
children.top_down_role: Two-resolvent and reflected-resolvent inclusion geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Two Maximally Monotone Operators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Douglas–Rachford fixed-point geometry for a two-operator zero problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A,B:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximally monotone on a Hilbert space and let \(\gamma>0\). Define \(J_{\gamma A}=(I+\gamma A)^{-1}\), \(R_{\gamma A}=2J_{\gamma A}-I\), and analogously for \(B\). If
\[T=\tfrac12\bigl(I+R_{\gamma A}R_{\gamma B}\bigr),\]
then every \(z\in\operatorname{Fix}T\) yields \(x=J_{\gamma B}z\) satisfying \(0\in Ax+Bx\). Conversely, every solution \(x\) and every \(b\in Bx\cap(-Ax)\) generate the fixed point \(z=x+\gamma b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zeros of two maximally monotone operators correspond to shadows of fixed points of the averaged composition of their reflected resolvents.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(B\) are maximally monotone on a Hilbert space.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Douglas–Rachford ordering, shadow map, and converse fixed-point construction are consistent, but no source with a specific locator is provided.

children.title: Maximal-Monotone Plus Monotone-Lipschitz Inclusions
children.top_down_role: Forward-access geometry beyond cocoercivity.

knowledge_statements.title: Maximal-Monotone Plus Monotone-Lipschitz Inclusions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward-accessible monotone sum class without a cocoercivity assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A maximal-monotone plus monotone-Lipschitz inclusion on a Hilbert space \(H\) is the problem
\[\text{find }x\in H\text{ such that }0\in Ax+Bx,\]
where \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximally monotone and \(B:H\to H\) is everywhere defined, monotone, and \(L\)-Lipschitz for some \(L>0\):
\[\langle Bx-By,x-y\rangle\geq0,\qquad \|Bx-By\|\leq L\|x-y\|.\]
Unlike cocoercivity, these assumptions do not generally make \(I-\gamma B\) nonexpansive; splitting methods may therefore require an additional forward evaluation or an equivalent correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This class sums a maximally monotone operator with a single-valued monotone Lipschitz field, without assuming the stronger cocoercivity needed by ordinary forward–backward splitting.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{solve }0\in A x+B x\) under monotone-Lipschitz forward access to \(B\).

notation.meaning: Lipschitz constant of the forward operator

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf and correctly distinguishes monotone-Lipschitz access from cocoercivity, but the methodological boundary claim requires an authoritative source and locator.

children.title: Three-Operator Inclusions
children.top_down_role: Inclusion structures containing three operator components.

knowledge_statements.title: Three-Operator Inclusions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two resolvent-accessible operators and one cocoercive forward operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A three-operator inclusion on a Hilbert space \(H\) has the form
\[\text{find }x\in H\text{ such that }0\in Ax+Bx+Cx,\]
where \(A,B:H\rightrightarrows H\) are maximally monotone and \(C:H\to H\) is \(\beta\)-cocoercive for some \(\beta>0\). Its convex minimization specialization is
\[\min_{x\in H} f(x)+g(x)+h(x),\]
with \(A=\partial f\), \(B=\partial g\), and \(C=\nabla h\), where \(f,g\) are proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions and \(h\) is convex differentiable with cocoercive gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A three-operator inclusion combines two maximally monotone terms, typically handled by resolvents, with one cocoercive term available through forward evaluation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The selected definition kind and three-operator model fit the container, but neither the operator class nor its convex specialization has an inspectable citation.

children.title: Finite Multi-Operator Inclusions
children.top_down_role: Inclusion structures containing larger finite operator families.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Multi-Operator Inclusions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite sums of set-valued monotone terms with an optional forward term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m\geq1\). A finite multi-operator inclusion on a Hilbert space \(H\) is
\[\text{find }x\in H\text{ such that }0\in\sum_{i=1}^{m}A_i x+B x,\]
where each \(A_i:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximally monotone and \(B:H\to H\) is a specified single-valued monotone operator, commonly cocoercive or monotone-Lipschitz. Membership means that there exist \(a_i\in A_i x\) such that \(\sum_{i=1}^{m}a_i+Bx=0\). The case \(B=0\) gives a purely resolvent-based finite sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite multi-operator inclusion seeks one point whose selected operator values, together with an optional forward field, sum to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(A_i:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximally monotone for every \(i\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-sum definition is internally precise and appropriate for the leaf, but it lacks an authoritative source with a specific locator.

children.title: Product-Space Liftings
children.top_down_role: Lifted representations that separate multiple operator components.

knowledge_statements.title: Product-Space Liftings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal product-space representation of a finite maximally monotone sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space, let \(m\geq1\) be an integer, and let \(A_i:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximally monotone for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). Define \(\boldsymbol H=H^m\), \(\boldsymbol A=A_1\times\cdots\times A_m\), and the diagonal subspace \(D=\{(x,\ldots,x):x\in H\}\). Then
\[0\in\sum_{i=1}^{m}A_i x\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in\boldsymbol A\boldsymbol x+N_D(\boldsymbol x),\qquad \boldsymbol x=(x,\ldots,x).\]
For \(\boldsymbol x\in D\),
\[N_D(\boldsymbol x)=D^\perp=\left\{(u_1,\ldots,u_m)\in H^m:\sum_{i=1}^{m}u_i=0\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite sum of maximally monotone operators can be represented in the product space by the Cartesian product operator plus the normal cone to the consensus diagonal.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a Hilbert space and \(m\geq1\) is an integer.
\(A_i:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximally monotone for every \(i=1,\ldots,m\).

notation.meaning: Cartesian product of the component operators

children.title: Consensus Coupling Structures
children.top_down_role: Coupling relations used to reconcile duplicated variables in lifted models.

knowledge_statements.title: Consensus Coupling Structures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graph-incidence representation of agreement and dual balance in product space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a connected finite graph with \(|V|=m\), choose an orientation, and let \(K:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^{|E|}\) be its vertex-to-edge incidence operator. Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(\boldsymbol x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\in H^m\), and let each \(A_i:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximally monotone. Then
\[(K\otimes I_H)\boldsymbol x=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x_1=\cdots=x_m.\]
Moreover,
\[0\in(A_1\times\cdots\times A_m)\boldsymbol x+N_{\ker(K\otimes I_H)}(\boldsymbol x)\]
holds if and only if there exists \(\lambda\in H^{|E|}\) such that
\[0\in(A_1\times\cdots\times A_m)\boldsymbol x+(K^*\otimes I_H)\lambda,\qquad (K\otimes I_H)\boldsymbol x=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a connected finite graph, its incidence constraint forces all vertex variables to agree, and adjoint-incidence multipliers represent the normal vectors that balance the local maximally monotone operators.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a connected finite graph with \(|V|=m\).
\(K:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^{|E|}\) is a vertex-to-edge oriented incidence operator.
\(A_i:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximally monotone for every \(i=1,\ldots,m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ker(K\otimes I_H)=\{(x,\ldots,x):x\in H\}\), and \(N_{\ker(K\otimes I_H)}(\boldsymbol x)=\operatorname{ran}(K^*\otimes I_H)\) for \(\boldsymbol x\) in this kernel.

notation.meaning: identity operator on the base Hilbert space

children.title: Operator-Count Scaling Boundaries
