children.title: Legendre Geometries
children.top_down_role: Bregman proximal settings generated by Legendre kernels.

assumptions_latex: \(X=\mathbb R^n\) and \(h:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A Legendre function is both essentially smooth and essentially strictly convex.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Legendre kernels used to generate Bregman proximal geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(h\) is Legendre when it is essentially smooth and essentially strictly convex: it is differentiable throughout \(\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}h)\), its gradient norm diverges along every interior sequence approaching a boundary point of \(\operatorname{dom}h\), and it is strictly convex on every convex subset of \(\operatorname{dom}\partial h\). For \(x\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}h)\), the induced Bregman divergence is \[D_h(y,x)=h(y)-h(x)-\langle\nabla h(x),y-x\rangle.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Legendre kernel is essentially smooth and essentially strictly convex, and its gradient generates a Bregman divergence on the interior of its domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Legendre Geometries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-dimensional definition matches Legendre Geometries and distinguishes essential smoothness from essential strict convexity. The record has no citation for these technical definitions or the associated Bregman divergence domain, so an authoritative convex-analysis source with a definition or page locator is required.

children.title: Entropy Geometries
children.top_down_role: Bregman proximal settings generated by entropy-type kernels.

assumptions_latex: \(h:\mathbb R_+^n\to\mathbb R\) is the negative Boltzmann-Shannon entropy with the convention \(0\log0=0\).
The Bregman base point satisfies \(x\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The induced divergence is generalized Kullback-Leibler divergence.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Negative-entropy Bregman geometry on the nonnegative orthant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(h(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n(x_i\log x_i-x_i)\), one has \(\nabla h(x)=(\log x_i)_{i=1}^n\) on \(\mathbb R_{++}^n\). Its Bregman divergence is \[D_h(y,x)=\sum_{i=1}^n\left(y_i\log\frac{y_i}{x_i}-y_i+x_i\right),\qquad y\in\mathbb R_+^n.\] If \(x\) and \(y\) belong to the probability simplex, the linear terms cancel and \(D_h(y,x)=\sum_i y_i\log(y_i/x_i)\), the usual relative entropy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative entropy generates generalized Kullback-Leibler divergence, which reduces to ordinary relative entropy on the probability simplex.
knowledge_statements.title: Entropy Geometries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits Entropy Geometries, and the displayed generalized Kullback–Leibler divergence is consistent with the stated entropy kernel and simplex specialization. A specific source locator is required because no citation supports the representation.

children.title: Entropy-as-Legendre Regime
children.top_down_role: Placement of entropy kernels within broader Legendre geometry.

assumptions_latex: \(h(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n(x_i\log x_i-x_i)\) on \(\mathbb R_+^n\), extended by \(+\infty\) outside \(\mathbb R_+^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The negative-entropy kernel is Legendre, with \(\nabla h(x)=\log x\) and \(\nabla h^*(s)=\exp s\).

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugate of the entropy kernel

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Negative entropy as a concrete Legendre kernel with explicit dual coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The negative-entropy kernel is strictly convex and differentiable on \(\mathbb R_{++}^n\), and \(\|
abla h(x^k)\|	o\infty\) whenever an interior sequence approaches the boundary of \(\mathbb R_+^n\). Hence it is Legendre. Moreover, \[h^*(s)=\sum_{i=1}^n e^{s_i},\qquad 
abla h(x)=\log x,\qquad 
abla h^*(s)=\exp s.\] Thus \(
abla h\) maps \(\mathbb R_{++}^n\) bijectively onto \(\mathbb R^n\), with inverse \(
abla h^*\), placing entropy geometry within the Legendre regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative entropy is a Legendre kernel: logarithms give its primal-to-dual coordinates, exponentials give the inverse map, and gradients diverge at the orthant boundary.
knowledge_statements.title: Entropy-as-Legendre Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property is well matched to Entropy-as-Legendre Regime and gives the expected conjugate and gradient coordinate maps. The Legendre classification, boundary-gradient behavior, and conjugacy formulas remain unsupported by any cited source; an authoritative source with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Asymmetric-Distance Boundary
children.top_down_role: Structural changes caused by losing Euclidean symmetry.

assumptions_latex: \(h\) is differentiable and strictly convex on the open convex set \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_h(x,y)\neq D_h(y,x)\) may hold, and left and right Bregman proximal maps need not coincide.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: follows directly from the standard Bregman-divergence definition; an exact authoritative locator is still required
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes Bregman proximity from symmetric metric proximity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x,y\in U\), define \(D_h(x,y)=h(x)-h(y)-\langle\nabla h(y),x-y\rangle\). In general, \(D_h(x,y)\neq D_h(y,x)\), and \(D_h\) need not satisfy a triangle inequality. Consequently, the two regularizations \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in U}\left\{f(x)+\lambda^{-1}D_h(x,y)\right\}\quad\text{and}\quad \operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in U}\left\{f(x)+\lambda^{-1}D_h(y,x)\right\}\] are structurally different and may have different domains, minimizers, and optimality conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Bregman divergence is generally asymmetric and nonmetric, so reversing its arguments can change the proximal problem, its domain, and its minimizers.
knowledge_statements.title: Asymmetric-Distance Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind and statement fit the asymmetric Bregman-distance container, but the record has no citation. An authoritative source with a specific definition, section, theorem, or page locator is required for the asymmetry, triangle-inequality failure, and distinction between left and right proximal constructions.

children.title: Finite-Dimensional Regimes
children.top_down_role: Euclidean proximal and inclusion settings.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}\) is everywhere defined, single-valued, and firmly nonexpansive.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical finite-dimensional proximal-mapping theorem; exact source locator pending
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical convex proximity on finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the problem \[\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(y)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{f(x)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\|x-y\|^2\right\}\] has a unique minimizer. Moreover, for all \(y,z\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \[\|\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(y)-\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(z)\|^2\leq \left\langle\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(y)-\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(z),y-z\right\rangle.\] Thus the proximal mapping has full domain and is firmly nonexpansive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper closed convex function on Euclidean space has an everywhere-defined, unique, firmly nonexpansive proximal mapping.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Dimensional Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem is mathematically standard and correctly restricted to finite-dimensional Euclidean space, and its content kind fits the container. The record nevertheless supplies no inspectable citation for existence, uniqueness, full domain, and firm nonexpansiveness.

children.title: Hilbert-Space Regimes
children.top_down_role: Possibly infinite-dimensional Hilbert-space settings.

assumptions_latex: \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and \(\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}=(I+\lambda\partial f)^{-1}\) is an everywhere-defined firmly nonexpansive mapping on \(H\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical Hilbert-space resolvent theorem for convex subdifferentials; exact source locator pending
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infinite-dimensional Hilbert-space form of classical convex proximity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(y\in H\), there is a unique \(x\in H\) satisfying \(0\in\partial f(x)+\lambda^{-1}(x-y)\). Hence \[\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(y)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in H}\left\{f(x)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\|x-y\|^2\right\}=(I+\lambda\partial f)^{-1}(y).\] For all \(y,z\in H\), this mapping satisfies \[\|\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(y)-\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(z)\|^2\leq\langle\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(y)-\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(z),y-z\rangle.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hilbert-space convex proximal maps remain everywhere defined, unique, and firmly nonexpansive, and equal subdifferential resolvents.
knowledge_statements.title: Hilbert-Space Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Hilbert-space theorem and resolvent identity fit the exact container and are stated with appropriate hypotheses, but no source reference or specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Dimension-Sensitive Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Topological and compactness distinctions between the ambient-space regimes.

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space with an orthonormal sequence \((e_k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The closed unit ball of \(H\) is not norm compact, although bounded sequences admit weakly convergent subsequences.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical orthonormal-sequence boundary between finite-dimensional compactness and Hilbert weak compactness
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates finite-dimensional norm compactness from infinite-dimensional weak compactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The sequence \((e_k)\) lies in the closed unit ball and satisfies \(\|e_j-e_k\|=\sqrt{2}\) whenever \(j\neq k\). It therefore has no norm-convergent subsequence, while \(e_k\rightharpoonup 0\). Thus boundedness yields norm-precompactness in finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces but not in infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. Proximal existence or convergence arguments using compact sublevel sets must consequently be replaced by weak compactness, weak lower semicontinuity, or coercivity arguments in the Hilbert regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In infinite-dimensional Hilbert space, bounded sequences need not have strongly convergent subsequences; proximal arguments must often use weak compactness instead.
knowledge_statements.title: Dimension-Sensitive Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The orthonormal-sequence example accurately expresses the dimension-sensitive compactness boundary and the failure-boundary kind is appropriate. A source with a specific locator is still required for the norm-noncompactness and weak-compactness assertions.

children.title: Banach-Space Resolvent Interface
children.top_down_role: The boundary with duality-mapping-based generalized resolvents.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a smooth reflexive Banach space whose normalized duality map \(J:X\to X^*\) is single-valued.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Banach generalized resolvent is \(R_{\lambda A}=(J+\lambda A)^{-1}J\), rather than \((I+\lambda A)^{-1}\).

notation.meaning: normalized duality mapping from X to its dual
set-valued operator from X to its dual

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard duality-mapping resolvent representation; geometric hypotheses for global single-valuedness require source certification
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Duality-map replacement of the Hilbert identity resolvent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in X\), a point \(u\in X\) belongs to \(R_{\lambda A}(x)\) exactly when \[Jx\in Ju+\lambda A(u),\] equivalently, when \(0\in A(u)+\lambda^{-1}(Ju-Jx)\). Hence \[R_{\lambda A}=(J+\lambda A)^{-1}J.\] In a Hilbert space identified with its dual, \(J=I\), and this reduces to \((I+\lambda A)^{-1}\). Outside Hilbert geometry, firm nonexpansiveness must be reformulated through the duality pairing or an associated Bregman functional.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Banach-space generalized resolvents replace the Hilbert identity by a duality map, changing both the inclusion and the appropriate nonexpansiveness geometry.
knowledge_statements.title: Banach-Space Resolvent Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the Banach-space resolvent interface, and the displayed inclusion is internally consistent. No cited source certifies the precise duality-map conventions, required Banach geometry, or the scope of the comparison with Hilbert-space firm nonexpansiveness.

children.title: Weakly Convex Proximal Regime
children.top_down_role: Restricted-scale proximal regularization beyond convexity.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex.
\(0<\lambda<\rho^{-1}\), with \(\rho=0\) interpreted as no upper restriction.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard restricted-scale theorem for weakly convex functions; exact source locator pending
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global Euclidean result below the weak-convexity threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Weak convexity means that \(x\mapsto f(x)+(\rho/2)\|x\|^2\) is convex. For every \(y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the function \[x\mapsto f(x)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\|x-y\|^2\] is \((\lambda^{-1}-\rho)\)-strongly convex and has a unique minimizer \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(y)\). The envelope \[f_\lambda(y)=\min_x\left\{f(x)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\|x-y\|^2\right\}\] is continuously differentiable and satisfies \(\nabla f_\lambda(y)=\lambda^{-1}(y-\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(y))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Below the reciprocal weak-convexity modulus, proximal subproblems are strongly convex, the proximal map is unique, and the Moreau envelope is smooth.
knowledge_statements.title: Weakly Convex Proximal Regime

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Prox-regularity is the stated uniform local quadratic lower-support inequality around \((\bar x,\bar v)\).

children.title: Local Proximal Regimes
children.top_down_role: Neighborhood-restricted proximal behavior and solution recovery.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is prox-bounded, prox-regular, and subdifferentially continuous at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\).
\(\bar z=\bar x+\lambda\bar v\), with \(\lambda>0\) sufficiently small.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An attentive localization of \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}\) is single-valued and Lipschitz near \(\bar z\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard local proximal-mapping theorem for prox-regular functions; exact parameter and localization statement needs authoritative checking
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attentive local mapping near a prox-regular graph point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For all sufficiently small \(\lambda>0\), there are neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar z\) and \(V\) of \(\bar x\) such that the attentive localization \[P_\lambda(z)=\left\{x\in V:x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_u\left(f(u)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\|u-z\|^2\right),\ |f(x)-f(\bar x)|\text{ is small}\right\}\] is single-valued and Lipschitz on \(U\), with \(P_\lambda(\bar z)=\bar x\). This is a local assertion and does not imply global uniqueness of proximal points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a prox-regular point and for small steps, the relevant localized proximal branch is single-valued and Lipschitz, without guaranteeing global uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Proximal Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind is suitable, but the condition that |f(x)-f(\bar x)| is 'small' is not quantified, and the exact relationship between the attentive local branch and the global argmin requires authoritative verification. The parameter range and localization theorem cannot be certified without a specific source locator.

children.title: Local Single-Valuedness Boundary
children.top_down_role: Transition between locally stable proximal selections and set-valued behavior.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The proximal model is uniquely solvable only for \(\lambda<\rho^{-1}\); at and above the threshold, single-valuedness or existence fails.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit quadratic calculation gives the sharp weak-convexity threshold
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp one-dimensional obstruction at the reciprocal curvature scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For center \(y\in\mathbb{R}\), the proximal objective is \[f_\rho(x)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}(x-y)^2=\frac12(\lambda^{-1}-\rho)x^2-\lambda^{-1}yx+\frac{y^2}{2\lambda}.\] If \(\lambda<\rho^{-1}\), it has the unique minimizer \(x=y/(1-\rho\lambda)\). If \(\lambda=\rho^{-1}\), every \(x\) minimizes when \(y=0\), while the objective is unbounded below when \(y\neq0\). If \(\lambda>\rho^{-1}\), it is unbounded below. Thus the scale restriction is sharp.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative quadratic shows the threshold is sharp: uniqueness holds below it, while at or above it the proximal problem becomes multivalued or unattained.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Single-Valuedness Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The calculation is correct as a sharp global weak-convexity threshold counterexample, but it does not describe the local single-valuedness boundary for an attentive proximal branch in the prox-regular local-geometry container. It belongs with the weakly convex proximal regime rather than this immutable leaf.

children.title: Proximal Well-Posedness Failures
children.top_down_role: Failures of existence, uniqueness, finiteness, or global single-valuedness.

children.title: Convex Well-Posedness Failure Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Extended-value models lacking the standard convex well-posedness properties.

children.title: Improper Models
children.top_down_role: Extended-value models failing properness requirements.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct counterexample from the definition of a proper extended-real function
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused solely by an empty effective domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\equiv+\infty\) is convex and lower semicontinuous but is not proper because \(\operatorname{dom}f=\varnothing\). For every \(y\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(\lambda>0\), the proximal objective \[x\mapsto f(x)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\|x-y\|^2\] equals \(+\infty\) everywhere. It therefore has no minimizer in the extended-real optimization convention, and \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(y)=\varnothing\). Properness excludes this elementary well-posedness failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The everywhere-infinite convex function has empty domain, so every proximal problem is identically infinite and has no proximal point.
knowledge_statements.title: Improper Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample kind fits Improper Models, but the assertion that an identically +infinity objective has an empty argmin depends on the minimizer convention; under the literal equality definition of argmin it may instead return the whole domain. A cited convention or a reformulation in terms of the standard proximal map being undefined for an improper function is required.

children.title: Nonclosed Models
children.top_down_role: Models whose relevant epigraphical structure lacks closedness.

assumptions_latex: \(f=\delta_{(0,\infty)}\) on \(\mathbb{R}\), where \(\delta_C\) is the indicator of \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The proximal infimum is finite but is not attained, so \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(-1)=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: extended-real indicator of a set C

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit open-set indicator counterexample demonstrates failure of lower semicontinuity
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional failure when closedness is removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The indicator \(f=\delta_{(0,\infty)}\) is proper and convex but not lower semicontinuous. Its proximal problem at \(y=-1\) reduces to \[\inf_{x>0}\frac{1}{2\lambda}(x+1)^2.\] The infimum equals \(1/(2\lambda)\) and is approached as \(x\downarrow0\), but \(0\notin(0,\infty)\). Hence the infimum is not attained and \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(-1)=\varnothing\). Closedness of the model prevents this boundary-escape mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The indicator of an open convex set is convex but nonclosed; a nearest boundary point can be excluded, leaving the proximal infimum unattained.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonclosed Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The open-half-line indicator is a correct counterexample for the Nonclosed Models leaf, and the counterexample kind is appropriate. The record has no authoritative citation with a specific locator for the indicator-function and proximal-attainment conventions.

children.title: Unattained Models
children.top_down_role: Models with finite infimal behavior but no attaining point.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The convex quadratic model \(f(x)+(1/2)\langle Qx,x\rangle\) has a finite infimum but no minimizer in \(\ell^2\).

notation.meaning: infinite-dimensional Hilbert space of square-summable sequences

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit noncoercive diagonal quadratic illustrates finite but unattained generalized proximal infimum
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infinite-dimensional nonattainment under a noncoercive proximal metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\Phi(x)=-\langle b,x\rangle+\frac12\langle Qx,x\rangle=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\left(\frac{x_n^2}{2n^2}-\frac{x_n}{n^2}\right).\] Coordinatewise minimization requires \(x_n=1\) for every \(n\), but the sequence \((1,1,\ldots)\) does not belong to \(\ell^2\). Truncations \(x^{(k)}=(1,\ldots,1,0,\ldots)\) show that \(\inf_{x\in\ell^2}\Phi(x)=-(1/2)\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}n^{-2}\), yet no \(x\in\ell^2\) attains it. The failure results from loss of metric coercivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive but noncoercive quadratic metric on an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space can yield a finite proximal infimum with no minimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Unattained Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The diagonal calculation correctly yields a finite unattained convex quadratic infimum and fits an unattained-model counterexample. A source is required to certify its placement as a generalized proximal failure, since the quadratic term is induced by a noncoercive operator rather than the standard Hilbert norm proximal regularizer.

children.title: Well-Posedness Failure Interactions
children.top_down_role: Overlap among improperness, nonclosedness, and unattainment.

knowledge_statements.title: Well-Posedness Failure Interactions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates impropriety, nonclosedness, and nonattainment for extended-real proximal models, including nonconvex models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\lambda>0\), \(x\in\mathbb R\), and \(q_x(y)=f(y)+(2\lambda)^{-1}|y-x|^2\), and call \(y\) a proximal solution only when it minimizes \(q_x\) with finite objective value. If \(f\equiv+\infty\), then \(q_x\) is improper and has no finite proximal solution. The proper convex function \(f(y)=0\) for \(y>0\) and \(f(y)=+\infty\) otherwise is not lower semicontinuous and, at \(x=0\), has infimum \(0\) with no minimizer. Conversely, the continuous proper nonconvex function \(f(y)=-y^4\) is closed but makes \(q_x\) unbounded below. Thus impropriety, nonclosedness, and nonattainment are distinct failure properties outside the proper closed convex setting.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Impropriety, nonclosedness, and nonattainment are distinct. An open-domain convex model can have an unattained proximal infimum, while a closed nonconvex model can fail through unboundedness below.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Impropriety, nonclosedness, and nonattainment are distinct failure properties.}
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit elementary extended-real examples distinguish the failure modes

children.title: Coercivity-Uniqueness Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Loss of coercivity or uniqueness outside the standard regime.

children.title: Unbounded Proximal Models
children.top_down_role: Proximal models lacking sufficient coercive control.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows failure when negative growth dominates proximal quadratic regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(y)=-y^4\). For every \(x\in\mathbb R\) and \(\lambda>0\), the proximal objective is \(q_x(y)=-y^4+(2\lambda)^{-1}(y-x)^2\). Since \(q_x(y)\to-\infty\) as \(|y|\to\infty\), its infimum is \(-\infty\) and no proximal point exists. Hence quadratic regularization does not make an arbitrary extended-real model bounded below; a lower-growth or convexity hypothesis is essential.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The model minus the fourth power overwhelms every quadratic proximal penalty, so the proximal objective is unbounded below and has no minimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Proximal Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quartic counterexample and its nonconvex scope are mathematically correct and fit the failure container, but no inspectable citation is supplied.

children.title: Multivalued Proximal Models
children.top_down_role: Proximal models admitting multiple proximal selections.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: stationary-point calculation for a coercive quartic
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Demonstrates loss of proximal uniqueness after convexity is removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(y)=(y^2-1)^2\), use parameter \(\lambda=1\), and evaluate at \(x=0\). The proximal objective equals \(y^4-\tfrac32y^2+1\). Its global minimizers are \(y=\pm\sqrt{3}/2\), whereas \(y=0\) is not a minimizer. Consequently \(\operatorname{Prox}_{f}(0)=\{-\sqrt{3}/2,\sqrt{3}/2\}\), so coercivity and attainment alone do not make the proximal mapping single-valued when convexity is absent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coercive nonconvex quartic has two proximal minimizers at the origin, showing that existence does not imply a single-valued proximal mapping.
knowledge_statements.title: Multivalued Proximal Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The objective and its two global minimizers are correct, and counterexample is the appropriate knowledge kind. No inspectable source is supplied.

children.title: Coercivity–Uniqueness Boundary
children.top_down_role: Distinctions between escape behavior and nonunique proximal responses.

assumptions_latex: X\text{ is a finite-dimensional Hilbert space}
f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\text{ exists uniquely for every }x\in X.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard finite-dimensional proximal well-posedness theorem
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional boundary separating existence from uniqueness of proximal points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\in X\), the function \(q_x(y)=f(y)+(2\lambda)^{-1}\|y-x\|^2\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, coercive, and \(\lambda^{-1}\)-strongly convex. It therefore attains its minimum at exactly one point, denoted \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\). Coercivity and lower semicontinuity supply existence, while strict convexity supplies uniqueness. Removing the growth conditions can destroy existence, and removing convexity can preserve attainment while producing several minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper closed convex model in finite dimensions, the proximal quadratic gives coercivity and strict convexity, hence existence and uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.title: Coercivity–Uniqueness Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-dimensional proper lower-semicontinuous convex hypotheses suffice for existence and uniqueness, and failure_boundary fits the leaf. An authoritative proximal-analysis citation with a precise locator is missing.

children.title: Termwise-Sum Failures
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by unsupported componentwise proximal evaluation of sums.

knowledge_statements.title: Termwise-Sum Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Refutes termwise evaluation of a proximal mapping for a sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(y)=g(y)=\tfrac12y^2\) on \(\mathbb R\), use unit proximal parameter, and let \(x\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}\). Then \(\operatorname{prox}_{f}(x)=\operatorname{prox}_{g}(x)=x/2\), while \(\operatorname{prox}_{f+g}(x)=x/3\). Consequently, \(\operatorname{prox}_{f+g}(x)\neq\operatorname{prox}_{f}(x)+\operatorname{prox}_{g}(x)=x\), and \(\operatorname{prox}_{f}(\operatorname{prox}_{g}(x))=x/4\neq x/3\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every nonzero scalar input, two equal quadratic terms show that the proximal map of a sum is neither the sum nor the sequential composition of the individual proximal maps.

children.title: Overlapping-Block Failures
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by coupling across nonseparable variable blocks.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit solution of two positive-definite linear systems
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows why overlapping blocks cannot generally be processed independently.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(x=(1,0)\), solving the joint quadratic problem yields \(\operatorname{prox}_{f+g}(x)=(2/5,-1/5)\). Processing the overlapping terms sequentially gives \(\operatorname{prox}_{g}(\operatorname{prox}_{f}(x))=(1/3,-1/6)\), which is different. The discrepancy occurs because both terms act on the first coordinate, so the optimality conditions are coupled rather than block-separable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two quadratic terms sharing one coordinate produce coupled optimality equations; sequential blockwise proximal evaluation gives the wrong point.
knowledge_statements.title: Overlapping-Block Failures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Both quadratic calculations are correct and demonstrate the overlapping-block failure. No inspectable block-proximal citation is supplied.

children.title: Componentwise-Evaluation Boundary
children.top_down_role: Structural limits of decomposing proximal evaluations by terms or blocks.

assumptions_latex: X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\text{ is an orthogonal Hilbert product}
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard separability rule for proximal mappings
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundary for componentwise proximal evaluation on orthogonal product spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\), orthogonality gives \(\|y-x\|^2=\sum_{i=1}^m\|y_i-x_i\|^2\). Hence the proximal minimization separates into \(m\) independent problems and \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)=(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f_i}(x_i))_{i=1}^m\). This componentwise rule need not hold when terms share variables or when the quadratic metric has off-diagonal blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separable convex function under an orthogonal product metric has a componentwise proximal map; overlapping terms or coupled metrics cross the boundary.
knowledge_statements.title: Componentwise-Evaluation Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The componentwise formula is correct for a finite orthogonal product with the stated separability hypotheses, and theorem is an appropriate role for this boundary leaf. A precise authoritative citation is missing.

children.title: Composition-Metric Compatibility Failures

children.title: Linear-Composition Failures
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by unsupported proximal treatment of linear compositions.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Composition Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Refutes an unnormalized linear-composition lookup rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=Y=\mathbb R\), let \(Lx=2x\), let \(g(t)=\tfrac12t^2\), and use the unit proximal parameter. For every \(x\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}\), \((g\circ L)(y)=2y^2\) and \(\operatorname{prox}_{g\circ L}(x)=x/5\). However, \(x+L^*(\operatorname{prox}_g(Lx)-Lx)=-x\). Hence the unnormalized linear-composition lookup is invalid for this dilation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At every nonzero scalar input, a dilation by two disproves the naive unnormalized proximal composition formula.

children.title: Metric Compatibility Failures
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by applying specialized calculus in incompatible metrics.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit oblique metric projection calculation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that off-diagonal metrics invalidate Euclidean coordinatewise lookup.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\operatorname{prox}^{M}_{f}(x)=\mathop{\rm argmin}_{y}\{f(y)+\tfrac12\|y-x\|_M^2\}\). At \(x=(1,0)\), feasibility imposes \(y_1=0\), and minimizing the remaining quadratic gives \(y_2=1/2\). Therefore \(\operatorname{prox}^{M}_{f}(1,0)=(0,1/2)\), while the Euclidean projection is \((0,0)\). The off-diagonal metric entry couples the constrained and free coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An off-diagonal positive-definite metric turns a coordinate projection into an oblique projection, so the Euclidean proximal catalog gives the wrong result.
knowledge_statements.title: Metric Compatibility Failures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The metric matrix is positive definite and the oblique projection calculation is correct. The counterexample fits the exact failure container, but no inspectable variable-metric source is supplied.

children.title: Composition–Metric Compatibility Boundary
children.top_down_role: Interaction between linear structure and metric requirements.

knowledge_statements.title: Composition–Metric Compatibility Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized surjective composition formula under exact operator-metric compatibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be real Hilbert spaces. Let \(M:X\to X\) be bounded, self-adjoint, and strongly positive; let \(L:X\to Y\) be bounded and surjective; and suppose \(LM^{-1}L^*=\alpha I_Y\) for some \(\alpha>0\). For \(g\in\Gamma_0(Y)\), \(\lambda>0\), and \(x\in X\), define \(\operatorname{prox}^{M}_{\lambda h}(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in X}\{\lambda h(y)+\tfrac12\langle M(y-x),y-x\rangle\}\). Then \[\operatorname{prox}^{M}_{\lambda(g\circ L)}(x)=x+\alpha^{-1}M^{-1}L^*\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha\lambda g}(Lx)-Lx\bigr).\] Without the compatibility identity, the reduced proximal problem generally uses a non-Euclidean metric on \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For real Hilbert spaces, a bounded surjective linear map that is a scaled coisometry in a strongly positive metric admits the displayed closed composition formula; otherwise the reduced metric generally cannot be discarded.
assumptions_latex: M:X\to X\text{ is bounded, self-adjoint, and strongly positive}
L:X\to Y\text{ is bounded and surjective}

notation.meaning: proximal mapping in the metric induced by M
proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions on Y

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: normalized linear-composition formula in a compatible metric

children.title: Proximal Catalog Recognition Failures
